quotes.text: Your default start of day is midnight in your time zone
Enter your email to request access.
For connected accounts in certain countries,
The new start of day only takes effect at the new time.
The settings at the time of the original transaction also apply to the payout.

old_evidence.text: Your default start of day is UTC midnight

findings: November replaces the May default of UTC midnight except some APAC users with midnight in the user's time zone except some APAC users. It adds an email request for preview access and a new Dashboard route for changing the cutoff.

The November payout overview says connected accounts without full Dashboard access or under platform control use the platform cutoff and that the platform can customize connected-account cutoff in certain countries. Its linked, same-date Connect guide documents a separate country list and US connected-account private preview.
Both captures group automatic payouts by a customized local day and preserve transaction-time settings. A setting change takes effect at the new cutoff rather than immediately.
substantive_changes: Default cutoff, connected-account control criteria and a preview access-request path change materially in the new raw. The documented setup setting and destination have moved. The general activation and previous-transaction rules carry forward.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Keep May wording for UTC default with APAC exceptions, Express/Custom and the old Dashboard route dated. Preserve the listed automatic-payout availability and examples under their own assumptions. Keep both direct and connected-account coverage distinct.
conflicts: The summary lines 18–19 and payout concept line 64 carry the May default and Express/Custom wording. November supplies a local-midnight default with APAC exceptions and a Dashboard access/platform-control test plus a country-scoped customization route.

The existing summary line 22 and concept line 64 make UTC retention universal. Both guides state the general rule that the original transaction's settings remain operative; UTC is the example's original time zone.

The direct payouts guide's country list includes PH. The Connect guide's separately scoped list omits PH and adds a private preview note for US connected accounts. The payouts guide’s New York example and unqualified email request do not establish US standard availability or an expanded direct preview country list.
unresolved_questions: The direct preview form does not identify covered countries, eligibility, approval or account rollout. The overview does not enumerate specific APAC default exceptions or guarantee bank receipt timing for other schedules.

source_assessments.reason: Date and update the default cutoff, connected-account scope, preview and Dashboard routing. Phrase previous payments in terms of original settings, and preserve both raw files and the reciprocal Stripe Payouts route.

answers.Q1: https://docs.stripe.com/payouts/customized-start-of-day explains cutoff-based grouping for reconciliation of automatic payouts. Stripe groups payments from one chosen local day into payout contents, illustrated by successive midnight or 06:00 Singapore cutoffs. The November capture says default midnight in the user's time zone, with some APAC exceptions, and usually permits a local-time range from midnight to morning. It lists AU, HK, ID, IN, JP, MY, NZ, PH, SG and TH, and offers an email request for preview access. Connected accounts lacking full Dashboard access or controlled by a platform use the platform's cutoff; eligible connected-account customization routes to the Connect guide (new raw lines 7–42). Merchants use Dashboard Settings → Linked accounts and payouts → Settlement and transfer rules → Start of day. The configured time becomes effective at the new cutoff, so a 07:00 Singapore-to-midnight change takes 17 hours in the example. Original transactions retain their original payout settings and timing, including already-grouped UTC Monday/Tuesday amounts in the example. Payments created after the change follow the new settings. Under the New York example's daily automatic and four-business-day assumptions, Monday's local-day sales arrive together before Friday ends (new raw lines 44–63). The May guide had the same list and timing examples but named UTC midnight with some APAC exceptions, Express/Custom with a common platform-chosen cutoff, and the prior Dashboard Business/Bank accounts and currencies path (old raw lines 8–29 and 31–50). source-stripe-payouts-start-of-day.md reflects those May details at lines 17–26, but line 22 should express original transaction settings generally, because UTC was the example's old setting.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payouts/customized-start-of-day, the 2026-11-07 local-midnight default with APAC exceptions replaces the 2026-05-11 UTC-midnight wording with APAC exceptions. The access/control-based connected-account rule and separate country-scoped customization route differ from the May Express/Custom account and common-cutoff phrasing, and the direct guide adds a preview email request (old raw lines 8–29 and 31–37, new raw lines 9–42). The Dashboard settings destination and labels change operational navigation (old raw lines 31–37, new raw lines 44–50); heading whitespace, numbering, screenshot hosting and formatting are presentational. The non-retroactive original-settings rule and effective-time examples still apply (old raw lines 39–46, new raw lines 52–59). The November Connect companion lines 9–31 links back to this guide for direct users and records its own connected-account coverage, omitting PH and identifying US connected-account private preview. The direct list still includes PH. Neither the direct preview form nor the New York illustration establishes US direct generally available or eligible. Update source-stripe-payouts-start-of-day.md lines 13–26, keep the May Raw Sources entry and add the November raw. Preserve its Stripe Payouts related link at line 30 and refresh the positions for the concept cutoff paragraph and Sources backlink at lines 64 and 89, along with the Stripe index entry at line 550. The root index links into Stripe at line 7 and the Stripe index concept entry remains at line 718.
